sentences.text: Velociraptor was a small dinosaur measuring between 1.5 and 2.07 meters in length and weighing between 14.1 and 19.7 kilograms, though some estimates suggest it could have reached lengths of about 2.5 meters and weighed up to 28 kilograms.
The animal possessed an elongated skull reaching a length of 23 centimeters and a large hand with three long fingers ending in curved claws that were structurally similar to modern bird wing bones.
Its most distinctive feature was an enlarged sickle claw on the second toe that could grow to over 6.5 centimeters in length and was likely used to restrain prey.
In 2007, researchers found six quill knobs on the ulna of a Velociraptor fossil from the Djadochta Formation, indicating the presence of feathers.
A 1971 fossil specimen shows a Velociraptor and a Protoceratops locked in combat, providing direct evidence of their predatory behavior.

A 1995 study reported a Velociraptor skull with two parallel rows of small holes in the frontal bones matching the size and spacing of Velociraptor teeth, suggesting a bite wound from another individual.
Fossil evidence shows that a bite wound on a Velociraptor skull did not heal, suggesting the injury likely caused the animal's death.
The genus Velociraptor was formally described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1924.
The first known Velociraptor fossil, a crushed complete skull with a manual claw, was discovered by Peter Kaisen on August 11, 1923, in the Gobi Desert.
Velociraptor was first described in 1924 and was initially classified in the family Megalosauridae.
The presence of feathers on Velociraptor suggests that larger flightless maniraptorans did not lose feathers secondarily because of their size.
Velociraptor feathers may have been used for display, nest brooding, or to aid in running up slopes.
Velociraptor could hear sound frequencies between 2,368 and 3,965 Hz, aiding in prey tracking.
Velociraptor had a bite force of 304 N, which is lower than that of Dromaeosaurus (885 N) and Deinonychus (706 N).
Velociraptor was warm-blooded to some degree due to the high energy requirements of hunting.
In 1995, researchers reported a Velociraptor skull with puncture wounds matching the spacing and size of Velociraptor teeth, suggesting an intraspecific fight.
Fossil evidence suggests Velociraptor was an opportunistic and active predator that also scavenged during droughts, famines, illness, or depending on the animal's age.
Velociraptor had an elongated snout indicating a selective feeding strategy of picking up small, fast prey.
Velociraptor is classified as a genus of small dromaeosaurid dinosaurs.
Velociraptor belongs to the group Eudromaeosauria, which is a subgroup of the family Dromaeosauridae.
The species Velociraptor osmolskae was named by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 2008.
Velociraptor lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
Velociraptor osmolskae lived alongside various species including Pinacosaurus, Linhenykus, Linheraptor, Machairasaurus, Bagaceratops, and others in the Bayan Mandahu Formation.
Specimens of Velociraptor mongoliensis have been recovered from the Djadochta Formation in the Mongolian province of Ömnögovi.
It is debated whether Velociraptor osmolskae belongs to the genus Velociraptor, as a 2013 study suggested it is closer to Linheraptor and may make the genus paraphyletic.
While it was once believed that Velociraptor's tail was stiff and rod-like, fossil evidence of an S-shaped tail suggests it had significant horizontal flexibility.
The "Fighting Dinosaurs" fossil is now thought to result from rapid burial by sand from a collapsing dune or sandstorm, rather than drowning.
